name: The Eyrie Vineyard
summary: The Lett family's founding vineyard in the Dundee Hills and the first of Eyrie's five estate sites, with plantings dated to 1965 and 1968.

name: Fault Line Vineyards
summary: Abacela's 76-acre estate vineyard near Roseburg, planted to Tempranillo and other varieties.

name: Cailloux Vineyard
summary: Cayuse's first vineyard, hand-planted to Syrah by Christophe Baron on 21 March 1997.

name: Shea Vineyard
summary: Yamhill-Carlton vineyard planted in 1989 by Dick Shea with about 140 acres of Pinot noir. Roughly 80 percent of its fruit is sold to other wineries for vineyard-designated bottlings.

sources.title: Shea Vineyard and Shea Wine Cellars (The Prince of Pinot)

name: Seven Springs Vineyard
summary: Eola-Amity Hills vineyard planted in 1984 by Al MacDonald, with additions in 1993-1995. Evening Land Vineyards took a 45-year lease on it in 2007.

sources.title: Evening Land Vineyards (The Prince of Pinot)
Seven Springs Vineyard collection, 2015 (Oregon Wine History Archive)

name: Ridgecrest Vineyards
summary: Vineyard planted by Harry Peterson-Nedry in 1980, the first in what became the Ribbon Ridge AVA, and the starting point for Chehalem winery.

name: Roserock Vineyard
summary: 279-acre Eola-Amity Hills property bought by the Drouhin family in 2013, planted mostly to Pinot noir.

sources.title: The French woman of Oregon, Véronique Drouhin-Boss (BKWine Magazine)

name: Maresh Vineyard
summary: Jim and Loie Maresh's vineyard on Worden Hill Road in the Dundee Hills, planted from 1970 and described as the fifth-oldest in Oregon.

sources.title: Vineyards Established 1965-1971 (The PinotFile / Prince of Pinot)
Maresh Red Barn (The Prince of Pinot)
Maresh Vineyard (¡Salud! Oregon Pinot Noir Auction)

name: Knudsen Vineyards
summary: Dundee Hills vineyard on a former walnut orchard bought by Cal and Julia Lee Knudsen in 1971, still owned by the Knudsen family. It has supplied Argyle Winery since 1987.

sources.title: Oregon Wine Pioneer Cal Knudsen Dies (Wine Spectator)
Knudsen Vineyards collection, 2024 (Oregon Wine History Archive)

name: Chehalem Mountain Vineyard
summary: Dick Erath's first vineyard, on Dopp Road near Newberg, planted in spring 1969 though often dated to 1968. Erath sold it in 1986.

sources.title: Vineyards Established 1965-1971 (The PinotFile / Prince of Pinot)
Dick Erath, Willamette Valley pioneer, passes away at 87 (Northwest Wine Report)
Erath Pinot Noir Clone 95: A Promising Oregon Suitcase Selection (The PinotFile / Prince of Pinot)
Pinot Noir "Clone 95": Dick Erath Revives an Old Treasure (The PinotFile / Prince of Pinot)

name: Prince Hill Vineyard
summary: Dundee Hills vineyard first planted by Dick Erath in 1983 and sold by him in 2017 to the owners of Silver Oak.

sources.title: Dick Erath, Willamette Valley pioneer, passes away at 87 (Northwest Wine Report)
Exclusive: Silver Oak Owners Buy Oregon Vineyard from Dick Erath (Wine Spectator)

name: Sokol Blosser Estate Vineyard
summary: The Sokol Blosser family's certified-organic estate in the Dundee Hills. The family bought the land, a former prune orchard, in 1970. Cuttings set out in a nursery row in 1971 were moved to the Old Vineyard in 1972.

sources.title: Vineyards Established 1965-1971 (The PinotFile / Prince of Pinot)

name: Temperance Hill Vineyard
summary: Organic, dry-farmed vineyard of about 90 acres at 660 to 880 feet in the Eola-Amity Hills, first planted in 1981 and owned by the Koo family of San Diego. Dai Crisp has managed it since 1999 and it sells fruit to more than two dozen wineries.

sources.title: 2014 Grower of the Year: Temperance Hill (Wine & Spirits Magazine)

name: Freedom Hill Vineyard
summary: Vineyard in the Coast Range foothills about ten miles southwest of Salem, planted by Dan and Helen Dusschee in the early 1980s and still family-owned. The original Pinot noir vines were lost to phylloxera and replanted from 2003.

sources.title: Vineyard: Freedom Hill (The Prince of Pinot)
Freedom Hill Vineyard collection, 2018 (Oregon Wine History Archive)
This is how you Start a Vineyard (Post Alley)

name: Hyland Vineyard
summary: Vineyard in the Coast Range foothills southwest of McMinnville, established in 1971 and described as the oldest commercial planting in the McMinnville AVA, with own-rooted Coury, Pommard and Wadenswil Pinot noir. Laurent and Danielle Andrus Montalieu and John Niemeyer bought it in 2007.

sources.title: Hyland Vineyard and King Estate (Great Northwest Wine)

name: Abbey Ridge Vineyard
summary: High-elevation Dundee Hills vineyard (650 to 800 feet) planted by Bill and Julia Wayne on a former prune orchard in the late 1970s. It is the oldest of the vineyards Cameron Winery draws on.

sources.title: Vineyard: Abbey Ridge (The Prince of Pinot)
Abbey Ridge Vineyard collection, 2023 (Oregon Wine History Archive)

name: Durant Vineyard
summary: Dry-farmed Dundee Hills vineyard of more than 60 acres established by Ken and Penny Durant in 1973. The family sold grapes to other wineries for decades and released its first Durant Vineyards wine in 2003.

sources.title: Ken and Penny Durant Interview (Oregon Wine History Archive, Linfield)
Durant Vineyards collection, 2025 (Oregon Wine History Archive)
Dundee Hills grape grower pioneers Oregon olive oil (Great Northwest Wine)

name: Zenith Vineyard
summary: Eola-Amity Hills vineyard originally planted by Pat O'Connor in the early 1980s as O'Connor Vineyard. Tim and Kari Ramey bought it in 2002, replanted the phylloxera-stricken vines and formed Zenith Vineyard LLC with St. Innocent's Mark Vlossak in 2006.

sources.title: Zenith Vineyard collection, 2024 (Oregon Wine History Archive)

name: Carter Vineyard
summary: Eola-Amity Hills vineyard about ten miles west of Salem, planted in 1983 by Jack and Kathleen Carter. Ken Wright Cellars managed it for the Carters. Ken Wright bought it from them in 2015. It is now owned by Ken and Karen Wright.

sources.title: Panther Creek Cellars Carter Vineyard Pinot Noir (Great Northwest Wine)
Panther Creek Cellars 2014 Carter Vineyard Pinot Noir, Eola-Amity Hills, $65 (Great Northwest Wine)
Ken Wright Cellars (The Prince of Pinot)

name: Canary Hill Vineyard
summary: Eola-Amity Hills vineyard founded by Nancy Daniel, with first vines planted in 1983. Nancy and Dick Daniel sold it to Ken Wright in 2006.

sources.title: Nancy Daniel interview photograph (Oregon Wine History Archive, Linfield)
Canary Hill Vineyards collection, 2017 (Oregon Wine History Archive)

name: Guadalupe Vineyard
summary: Vineyard planted in 1989 on Willakenzie soils and owned by Jim Stonebridge and Kathleen Boeve. It is one of Ken Wright Cellars' single-vineyard Pinot noir sites.

name: Momtazi Vineyard
summary: Biodynamic vineyard in the McMinnville AVA on a former wheat farm that Moe and Flora Momtazi bought in 1997. Planting began in March 1998 with 13 acres of Pommard-clone Pinot noir and has grown to more than 200 acres.

sources.title: Moe and Hanna Momtazi interview photograph (Oregon Wine History Archive, Linfield)

name: Elton Vineyard
summary: Eola-Amity Hills vineyard planted in 1983 by Dick and Betty O'Brien on land Betty inherited, and named for her father, Elton Ingram. When the O'Briens retired in 2007 it went under long-term lease to Willamette Valley Vineyards.

sources.title: Elton Vineyards collection, 2015 (Oregon Wine History Archive)

name: Resonance Vineyard
summary: Own-rooted, biodynamically farmed vineyard in the Yamhill-Carlton AVA first planted to Pinot noir in 1981 by Kevin and Carla Chambers, who sold the fruit for about 20 years before starting their own label in 2006. Maison Louis Jadot bought it in August 2013.

sources.title: Burgundy's Louis Jadot Purchases Oregon Pinot Noir Vineyard (Wine Spectator)

name: Quail Run Vineyards
summary: Rogue Valley vineyards farmed by the Moore family since 1989, known for warm-climate reds such as Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot and Syrah. The fruit goes into Willamette Valley Vineyards' Griffin Creek label, and growers Don and Traute Moore also ran South Stage Cellars in Jacksonville.

sources.title: Wines of the Rogue Valley (Portrait Magazine / Great Northwest Wine)

name: Le Puits Sec Vineyard
summary: Evesham Wood's non-irrigated estate vineyard in the Eola-Amity Hills. Its first three acres of own-rooted Pommard-clone Pinot noir were planted in 1986.

sources.title: Erin Nuccio, Evesham Wood | Haden Fig (Eola-Amity Hills Winegrowers)

name: Stoller Estate Vineyard
summary: Vineyard on the Stoller family's former turkey farm, which Bill Stoller bought in 1993. He planted the first 10 acres each of Pinot noir and Chardonnay in 1995, and it now covers 225 acres.

name: Beacon Hill Vineyard
summary: Yamhill-Carlton vineyard with plantings dating to 1988. Tony and Michelle Soter bought it in 1997 as the first home of Soter Vineyards and sold it in 2005.

name: Brooks Estate Vineyard
summary: A 20-acre Eola-Amity Hills vineyard planted to Pinot noir and Riesling between 1973 and 1977. Jimi Brooks farmed it biodynamically from 2002, and Brooks later bought it; it was Demeter certified in 2012.

sources.title: Brooks Wine: The People of Brooks

name: Zena Crown Vineyard
summary: Eola-Amity Hills vineyard assembled by Jackson Family Wines, which bought the final parcel in May 2013. It is the source of the Zena Crown label.

sources.title: Jackson Family Continues Oregon Pinot Noir Expansion, Buying WillaKenzie Estate (Wine Spectator)

name: Seven Hills Vineyard
summary: Vineyard near Milton-Freewater on the Oregon side of the Walla Walla Valley, planted in the early 1980s by physicians James McClellan and Herb Hendricks. Crimson Wine Group bought its oldest blocks in 2016, reuniting them with Seven Hills Winery.

sources.title: Crimson Wine Group Buys 66 Acres of Walla Walla Valley Vines (Wine Spectator)

name: Vista Hills Vineyard
summary: Dundee Hills vineyard on Hilltop Lane in Dayton, at 670 to 870 feet. Francis Ford Coppola's wine company bought it in 2018; ROCO Winery acquired the 59-acre property, 41 acres of it under vine, in March 2026.

sources.title: Italian wine group acquires Dundee Hills vineyard from Coppola-owned Domaine Lumineux (Newsberg)

name: Watermill Estate Vineyard
summary: Watermill Winery's 13.25-acre vineyard in The Rocks District of Milton-Freewater, planted in 2006.

name: Red Hill Vineyard
summary: The only vineyard in the Red Hill Douglas County AVA, on red Jory soil at 800 to 1,200 feet. First planted in the late 1960s, it was expanded by Wayne Hitchings from seven acres in 1991 to about 450, and is the home of the Sienna Ridge Estate label.

sources.title: AVA Unto Its Own: Wayne Hitchings (Oregon Wine Press)
Red Hill Douglas County, Oregon AVA (Wikipedia)

name: Mae's Vineyard
summary: Quady North's estate vineyard in the Applegate Valley, planted by Herb Quady in 2006 to Viognier, Syrah and Cabernet franc.

sources.title: Herb Quady resigns from Troon Vineyard (Great Northwest Wine)

name: Doerner Vineyards
summary: Century-farm vineyard in the Melrose area of the Umpqua Valley, first planted by Adam Doerner in 1889 and still farmed by his descendants. It covered about 22 acres in 2018, including Zinfandel regrafted from the original plantings.

sources.title: Way-Back Wine: Doerner Vineyards (Oregon Wine Press)

name: David Hill Vineyard
summary: Hillside site west of Forest Grove, earlier known as Wine Hill or Reuter's Hill, where the Reuter family grew wine grapes before Prohibition; those vines were pulled and replaced with fruit trees and potatoes. Charles Coury replanted it from 1965 as the estate of Charles Coury Vineyards, and since 1992 it has belonged to Milan and Jean Stoyanov's David Hill Vineyards & Winery.

sources.title: Charles Coury and the Coury selection (Prince of Pinot)
David Hill Vineyard & Winery (Prince of Pinot)
David Hill Winery collection, 2020 (Oregon Wine History Archive)

name: Abetina Vineyard
summary: Ponzi Vineyards site in the Laurelwood District, planted by Dick Ponzi in 1975 alongside Oregon State University. It is listed with Madrona Vineyard in LIVE's certified-member directory.

sources.title: A Long Story, Still Being Told (Ponzi Vineyards)

name: Anahata Vineyard
summary: Roughly 24-acre vineyard surrounding the AtTheJoy estate in the Eola-Amity Hills, with eight blocks named for words meaning joy; the estate source for Aubaine and Lytle-Barnett.

name: Case Vineyard
summary: Organically farmed Chardonnay and Pinot noir vineyard near Newberg owned by Kathleen Keppinger, a fruit source for Jachter Family Wines.

sources.title: Former Oregon car dealer gears up with Jachter Family Wines (Great Northwest Wine)

name: Raindance Vineyard
summary: Vineyard owned by Ken Austin, who also owns The Allison Inn; source of Jachter Family Wines' Raindance Foothills Chardonnay.

name: Blackfeather Vineyard
summary: Estate vineyard of Greywing Wines, named for Johnson Blackfeather.

name: Lonesome Rock Vineyard
summary: High-elevation, ocean-influenced vineyard west of Carlton, just outside the Yamhill-Carlton AVA. Formerly the De Ponte Cellars owners' Lonesome Rock Ranch, it is now about 15 acres of Pinot noir, Chardonnay and Pinot Meunier and sells fruit to Corollary Wines.

name: Windfall Vineyard
summary: 117-acre vineyard on the west side of the Eola-Amity Hills, first harvested in 2024 for Aubaine.

name: Armstrong Vineyard
summary: Ribbon Ridge vineyard developed by Doug and Michele Ackerman and planted in 2007, mostly to Pinot noir; the sole fruit source for Red Electric.

name: Saffron Fields Vineyard
summary: Estate vineyard of Saffron Fields in the Yamhill-Carlton AVA, planted in 2007 on a former grass seed farm. It also supplies Pinot noir and Chardonnay to EIEIO & Company.

sources.title: Saffron Fields collection, 2020 (Oregon Wine History Archive)

name: White Cloud Vineyard
summary: Vineyard near the EIEIO farm, notable for vines trained in an umbrella-like shape rather than on a standard trellis; a fruit source for EIEIO.

name: Bayliss-Bower Vineyard
summary: Estate vineyard of Ghost Hill Cellars on the Bayliss family farm in Yamhill-Carlton, first planted with four acres of Pinot noir in 1999.

name: Le Cadeau Vineyard (estate)
summary: Vineyard on 28 acres of rocky, previously forested hillside on Parrett Mountain bought by Tom Mortimer in 1997; the first six acres of Pinot noir were planted in 1999 and it now holds 18 Pinot noir clones.

name: X Novo Vineyard
summary: Eola-Amity Hills vineyard that former Joseph Phelps winemaker Craig Williams and his wife Robin began planting in 2010, known for a Chardonnay block holding about fifteen clones.

name: X Omni Vineyard
summary: Craig Williams's second Eola-Amity Hills vineyard, planted a few years after neighbouring X Novo; it supplies Chardonnay and Pinot noir to a number of small producers.

name: Hope Well Vineyard
summary: Willamette Valley vineyard formerly owned and farmed by Mimi Casteel, now the Coulee Estate vineyard of Bledsoe|McDaniels.

name: Meredith Mitchell Vineyard
summary: Cool site of about 22 planted acres in the McMinnville AVA, with Pinot blanc vines dating from 1990. Fruit goes to Harper Voit and Elevee, among others; the property was listed for sale in 2021.

sources.title: Élevée Winegrowers, Meredith Mitchell Vineyard Pinot Noir 2021 (Decanter)

name: Bieze Vineyard
summary: Low-yielding rocky ridgetop vineyard in the Eola-Amity Hills near Seven Springs, supplying Pinot noir to Harper Voit and Big Table Farm.

name: de Lancellotti Estate Vineyard
summary: About 4.5 acres at the end of Calkins Lane, planted in the early 2000s and farmed biodynamically. Bergström Wines bottled fruit from the site until 2018.

name: Koosah Vineyard
summary: High-elevation Eola-Amity Hills vineyard at about 1,100 feet, developed by Kevin and Carla Chambers and sold to Resonance in early 2022.

name: Holstein Vineyard
summary: Holstein family vineyard planted in 1972, bottled as a vineyard designate by Purple Hands.

sources.title: Holstein Vineyards collection, 2017 (Oregon Wine History Archive)

name: Bunker Hill Vineyard
summary: Eola-Amity Hills Chardonnay site that supplied Lundeen Wines before Larry Stone bought it for Lingua Franca.

sources.title: Bunker Hill (The PinotFile / Prince of Pinot)
Exclusive: Constellation Buys Oregon's Lingua Franca (Wine Spectator)

name: Nysa Vineyard
summary: Densely planted 40-acre Dundee Hills vineyard established in 1990 by Michael Mega, bordering Domaine Drouhin, Archery Summit and Domaine Serene. Mega bottles long-aged estate wines and sells fruit to Audeant, Nicolas-Jay and Lavinea.

sources.title: Nysa Vineyard collection, 2023 (Oregon Wine History Archive)

name: Luminous Hills Vineyard
summary: Willamette Valley vineyard bottled as a single-vineyard Pinot noir by Audeant.

name: Lazy River Vineyard
summary: Vineyard on the south slope of Mount Richmond near Yamhill, with Pinot noir planted in 2000 and Chardonnay in 2005; a fruit source for Lavinea.

sources.title: Panther Creek Cellars 2014 Lazy River Vineyard Pinot Noir, Yamhill-Carlton (Great Northwest Wine)

name: Vista Grande Vineyard
summary: Chehalem Mountains vineyard at about 800 feet that supplies Pinot noir to de la boue.

name: Gregory Ranch Vineyard
summary: Biodynamically farmed Yamhill-Carlton vineyard that has supplied Bergström and now de la boue, whose winemaker Travis Todd farms it.

name: La Cantera Vineyard
summary: Vineyard at about 690 feet above the Rex Hill winery, source of a Lundeen single-vineyard Pinot noir.

name: Celestial Hill estate vineyard
summary: 52-acre property outside McMinnville with 12 acres of vines planted in the 1990s, known as Falcon Glen before Chris and Melissa Thomas bought it in 2020. Planted to Pinot noir, with some vines since grafted to Chardonnay.

name: Fennwood Vineyard
summary: Yamhill-Carlton vineyard that supplies Chardonnay to Celestial Hill. A Hampton Lumber subsidiary bought it in 2018 and kept supplying its winery customers, among them Dusky Goose.

sources.title: Hampton Purchases Fennwood Vineyard in Yamhill-Carlton (Hampton Lumber)

name: Orchard House Vineyard
summary: Organically farmed estate vineyard of Iterum Wines at Joe and Patricia Dobbes's home in the Eola-Amity Hills, planted to Pinot noir and Chardonnay.

name: Oak Grove Vineyard
summary: Sauvignon blanc source for Iterum Wines that Joe Dobbes first worked with in 1989.

name: Murto Vineyard
summary: Dundee Hills vineyard owned and farmed by Mike and Robin Murto, planted in 1978. Authentique makes a single-vineyard Pinot noir from it.

sources.title: Murto Vineyard collection (Oregon Wine History Archive)
Authentique Wine Cellars, Murto Vineyard Pinot Noir, Dundee Hills, Willamette Valley, Oregon, USA 2019 (Decanter)

name: Clos Gallia
summary: Domaine Divio's estate vineyard, planted by winemaker Bruno Corneaux around the tasting room near Newberg.

name: Abbott Claim Vineyard
summary: Vineyard on Savannah Ridge near Carlton, named for homesteader John F. Abbott. Ken Wright planted it to Pinot noir in 2001 and sold the land to Antony Beck in two stages, in 2006 and 2012; it is now the home vineyard of the Abbott Claim winery.

name: Bishop Creek Vineyard
summary: Organically farmed estate vineyard of Nicolas-Jay in the northern Yamhill-Carlton AVA, bought in 2014; mostly Pinot noir with a little Chardonnay.

name: Youngberg Hill Vineyard
summary: Estate vineyard of Youngberg Hill, about 21 acres. Its two oldest Pinot noir blocks, Natasha and Jordan, were planted in 1989 by Ken Wright for Panther Creek.

name: Namaste Vineyard
summary: Late-ripening vineyard planted in 1980 and farmed by Jessica Cortell; a Chardonnay source for Corollary's sparkling wines.

name: Winter's Hill Vineyard
summary: Estate vineyard of Winter's Hill in the Dundee Hills, first planted in 1990 on a former grass-seed field and since grown to about thirty-five acres.

sources.title: Oregon Wine Month feature: Winter's Hill Estate (1000 Friends of Oregon)
Bees, Birds and Pinot Take Center Stage at Winter's Hill Estate (Portland Monthly, sponsored)

name: Domingo Vineyard
summary: Vineyard at the foot of the Dundee Hills planted by Jesús Guillén Sr. and named after the family's grandfather; a fruit source for Guillén Family Wines.

name: Desiree Vineyard
summary: Fox Farm Vineyards' estate vineyard in the Dundee Hills, on the five acres of Jory soil and southeast-facing slope that David Fish and Desiree Neel bought with their home in 2007. Fox Farm bottles Desiree Estate Chardonnay and Pinot noir from it.

sources.title: David Fish of Fox Farm Vineyards (Fox Farm Vineyards)
Buy Fox Farm Vineyards wines (Fox Farm Vineyards)
Michael Arrington, 15 October 2026: Fox Farm Vineyards has its own estate vineyard, Desiree Vineyard

name: Claygate Vineyard
summary: Estate vineyard of Claygate Estate Vineyard, planted in 2008 on 3.25 acres of a 42-acre Ribbon Ridge property that was once part of a homestead fruit and nut farm.

name: Belle Pente Estate Vineyard
summary: Belle Pente's own hillside vineyard at 240 to 500 feet, first planted in 1994 on the site of an old Italian plum orchard. Over 16 acres of Pinot noir, Pinot gris, Chardonnay and a little Gamay, dry farmed to organic standards since 2000 by the winery's own crew.

name: Bella Vida Vineyard
summary: Dundee Hills vineyard that supplied Belle Pente's Willamette Valley Pinot noir from 2001 to 2018, then owned and managed by Steve and Allison Whiteside.

sources.title: Independent vineyards where we source our fruit (bellepente.com)

name: Rivenwood Vineyard
summary: 2.5-acre Yamhill-Carlton vineyard next to Belle Pente's estate, owned by Rick and Heather Karl and farmed by Belle Pente as an extension of its own vineyard.

sources.title: Independent vineyards where we source our fruit (bellepente.com)

name: Stag Hollow Vineyard
summary: Yamhill-Carlton vineyard owned and managed by Mark Huff and Jill Zarnowitz, a source of Early Muscat and Muscat Ottonel.

sources.title: Independent vineyards where we source our fruit (bellepente.com)
Stag Hollow Wines collection, 2022 (Oregon Wine History Archive)

name: Foxy Rock Vineyard
summary: Yamhill-Carlton vineyard owned by the Heilman family and managed by Chad Vargas.

sources.title: Independent vineyards where we source our fruit (bellepente.com)

name: Aileron Hill Vineyard
summary: Yamhill-Carlton vineyard owned by Ben and Lauren Powers and managed by Jose Arguelles.

sources.title: Independent vineyards where we source our fruit (bellepente.com)

name: Barakel Vineyard
summary: Vineyard planted by Dean Underwood, who decided what to plant and where to sell the grapes.

sources.title: Oral history interview with Dean Underwood, 2026 (Oregon Wine History Archive)
Barakel Vineyards collection, 2026 (Oregon Wine History Archive)

name: Celestina Vineyard
summary: Vineyard near Medford bought in 2004 by John and Sherry Pratt, planted in 2007 and first harvested in 2009.

sources.title: Oral history interview with John Pratt, 2026 (Oregon Wine History Archive)
Celestina Vineyard collection, 2026 (Oregon Wine History Archive)

name: Graves Vineyard
summary: Vineyard in Dallesport, Washington, started by Don Graves.

sources.title: Oral history interview with Don Graves, 2014 (Oregon Wine History Archive)
Graves Vineyard collection, 2014 (Oregon Wine History Archive)

name: Fayetta Vineyard
summary: Vineyard project started by Jacob Sembler near McMinnville.

sources.title: Fayetta Vineyard collection, 2022 (Oregon Wine History Archive)

name: Threemile Vineyard
summary: Vineyard in The Dalles in the Columbia Gorge region.

sources.title: Oral history interview with Joe Cushman, 2022 (Oregon Wine History Archive)
Threemile Vineyard collection, 2022 (Oregon Wine History Archive)

name: Pamar Vineyard
summary: Perrydale vineyard where Mark Bjornson has planted the rare grape Gouais Blanc.

sources.title: Oral history interview with Mark & Pattie Bjornson, 2024 (Oregon Wine History Archive)

name: Ruby Vineyard
summary: Vineyard where Andrew Kirkland works.

sources.title: Ruby Vineyard collection, 2022 (Oregon Wine History Archive)

name: West Wind Vineyard
summary: Vineyard bought by Piper Underbrink and Ben Stalker in 2021, the source of their Sealionne brand.

sources.title: Sealionne Wines collection, 2025 (Oregon Wine History Archive)
Westwind Vineyard / Privé Vineyard & Winery (Ribbon Ridge AVA winery directory)

name: Weber Vineyards
summary: Vineyard planted by the Weber family, who sold its grapes under Dick Erath's guidance.

sources.title: Oral history interview with Vivian Weber, 2019 (Oregon Wine History Archive)
Weber Vineyards collection, 2019 (Oregon Wine History Archive)

name: White Rose Vineyard
summary: Existing 10-acre vineyard that Greg Sanders bought in 2000, the start of White Rose Estate.

name: Looney Vineyard
summary: Seven-acre estate vineyard on Ribbon Ridge planted by Ed and Darlene Looney of Aramenta Cellars.

name: Bramble Hill Vineyard
summary: Pinot Noir vineyard on Ribbon Ridge near Newberg, not open to visitors. Its fruit goes into a vineyard-designated Penner-Ash Pinot Noir.

sources.title: Bramble Hill Vineyard (Ribbon Ridge AVA winery directory)
Women of the Willamette Valley: Pioneering the Future (Scout Magazine)
2014 Penner-Ash Bramble Hill Vineyard Pinot Noir (Delectable)

name: Halliday Hill Vineyard
summary: Certified biodynamic Pinot Noir vineyard of about 1.5 acres on Ribbon Ridge, owned by Jim and Karen Halliday and farmed by Doug Tunnell of Brick House Vineyards; it calls itself the smallest commercial vineyard in the Willamette Valley.

sources.title: Halliday Hill (Ribbon Ridge AVA winery directory)

name: Le Pré du Col Vineyard
summary: Sixteen-acre Pinot Noir and Chardonnay vineyard on Ribbon Ridge planted by the Hill family from 2006 to 2011 and farmed biodynamically by Bergström Wines since 2008.

sources.title: Le Pré Du Col Vineyard (Ribbon Ridge AVA winery directory)

name: Meyerhofer Vineyard
summary: Three-acre Pinot Noir vineyard on the south end of Ribbon Ridge, planted in 2014 and leased to and farmed by neighboring Domaine Divio.

sources.title: Meyerhofer Vineyards (Ribbon Ridge AVA winery directory)

name: Belle Colline Vineyard
summary: Organically farmed Pinot noir and Chardonnay vineyard in the Chehalem Mountains, bought in 2016 by Danell and Kipp Myers as the estate of Anacréon Winery.

name: Battle Creek Vineyard
summary: Pinot noir vineyard of about 110 acres on a south-facing slope near Turner, southeast of Salem, planted in 1998 in small blocks on volcanic basalt soil; the namesake source for Battle Creek Cellars.

name: Warrior's Rest Vineyard
summary: Bellingar family estate vineyard on North Valley Road west of Newberg, on a farm settled in 1918 by Italian immigrant Louis Dare. The first phase of the current planting went in in 2017, with Chardonnay and Pinot noir.

name: Brigadoon Vineyards
summary: The Shown family's 66-acre organically farmed vineyard in the Lower Long Tom AVA northwest of Eugene, on a tributary of Ferguson Creek, home to Brigadoon Wine Co.

name: Tukwilla Vineyard
summary: Estate vineyard of Burton Bittman Wines in the middle of the Dundee Hills, begun in 1990 with seven acres of Pinot noir and since grown to about 19 acres including Pinot gris and Pinot blanc.

name: Geary Claim Vineyard
summary: Dundee Hills estate vineyard of Burton Bittman Wines, next to Tukwilla Vineyard on part of an early Oregon land claim that once grew fruit and walnuts. Pinot noir and Chardonnay were first planted there in 2017.

name: Wade Vineyard
summary: Small high-elevation vineyard in the Dundee Hills established by Lance Wade, now farmed by Burton Bittman Wines mainly for late-ripening Pinot gris.

name: Old Wagon Road Vineyard
summary: Estate vineyard of Chris James Cellars in the Coast Range foothills west of Carlton, first planted in 2013 and now about 25 acres of 16 varieties. Some of its fruit is sold to other wineries.

sources.title: Old Wagon Road Vineyard (Chris James Cellars)

name: Patton Valley Vineyard
summary: Gaston vineyard that Failla describes as its first Oregon estate vineyard and the home of its Oregon winery and tasting room.

name: Haakon/Lenai Vineyard
summary: High-slope Dundee Hills vineyard that Cody and Marque Wright acquired in 2018, the estate of their Haakon/Lenai wines.

name: Pelos Sandberg Vineyard
summary: Dry-farmed estate vineyard of iOTA Cellars in the Eola-Amity Hills, first planted in 2002 at 300 to 500 feet.

name: Finnigan Hill Vineyard
summary: Higher-elevation, organically farmed Pinot noir site in the Chehalem Mountains that supplies other producers' Willamette Valley blends.

sources.title: Bellande Pinot Noir Willamette Valley 2025 (Bowler Wine)
Finnigan Hill Vineyards (Willamette Valley Wineries Association member listing)

name: Inguz Row
summary: Five-acre vineyard and farm near 900 feet on Chehalem Mountain, planted in 2012 and bought in 2020 by Mark and Charla Cain, who also grow lavender, olives and other crops. A first small release of their own Pinot noir and Chardonnay was announced as coming soon.

sources.title: Inguz Row Vineyard & Farm (Willamette Valley Wineries Association member listing)

name: Alchemy Vineyard
summary: Vineyard behind K & M Winery’s single-vineyard Pinot Noir, which carries the Chehalem Mountains appellation.

sources.title: K & M Winery Réserve Alchemy Vineyard Pinot Noir 2012 (Delectable)
K&M Wines, Alchemy Vineyard (Willamette Valley Wineries Association member listing)

name: Aegrina Vineyard
summary: Vineyard on a southwest-facing slope near McMinnville, in the McMinnville AVA, farmed since 2007. It is one of La Biblioteca's estate vineyards. It is also one of the two estate vineyards of North Valley Vineyards.

sources.title: Soter Vineyards Announces Sale of North Valley Brand (Wine Industry Advisor)

name: North Valley Vineyard
summary: Ten-acre vineyard on a southeast-facing slope in the Yamhill-Carlton AVA, planted in 2007 and one of La Biblioteca's estate vineyards. It is also an estate vineyard of North Valley Vineyards, next to Shea, Penner-Ash and Beaux Freres.

sources.title: Soter Vineyards Announces Sale of North Valley Brand (Wine Industry Advisor)

name: Lachini Estate Vineyard
summary: 45-acre biodynamically farmed estate of Lachini Vineyards on the southeastern edge of the Chehalem Mountains AVA, mostly Pinot Noir with some Chardonnay; the first five acres went in in 1999.

name: MonksGate Vineyard
summary: 20-acre Yamhill-Carlton vineyard of the Moore family beside a Trappist abbey, planted from 2000 to 2007, which supplies the MonksGate label and contracting wineries.

name: Tidalstar Vineyard
summary: 30-acre vineyard on the western edge of the Yamhill-Carlton AVA, planted in 1999 and bought by Montinore Estate in 2016, which converted it to biodynamic farming.

name: Laughlin Road Ranch
summary: Farm in northeastern Yamhill-Carlton that Montinore Estate bought in 2019 and planted to vines; its first harvest was in 2023.

name: Tuscowallame Vineyard
summary: Raptor Ridge Winery's estate vineyard in the Chehalem Mountains; its name is glossed as a native word for where owls live.

name: Redhawk Vineyard
summary: 23-acre estate vineyard of RH Wines in the Eola-Amity Hills, west of Salem.

name: Roots Estate Vineyard
summary: Estate vineyard of Roots Wine Co. in the Yamhill-Carlton AVA, established in 1999 and 2000.
